idiom_name: PORO service object with a single .call + ActiveRecord::Base.transaction
implementation_notes: Rails supplies the transaction block - ActiveRecord::Base.transaction, with ActiveRecord::Rollback as the silent-rollback signal and after_commit callbacks for work that must happen only once the data is visible - and nothing for the layer itself. The convention is a plain old Ruby object per operation (Orders::Place, Tasks::Create), exposing only .call and receiving collaborators through the constructor; ActiveRecord models stay the domain objects. The service class is not replaced, just reduced to one public method; the structure is justified when a use case touches several models and external systems, while a single-model operation is idiomatic as a model method with a transaction block.
code_sketch:
class Orders::Place
  def initialize(customer:, items:, gateway: Payments)
    @customer, @items, @gateway = customer, items, gateway
  end
  def call
    ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
      order = @customer.orders.create!(items: @items)
      @gateway.charge(order)          # raises => ROLLBACK
      order
    end
  end
end
pitfalls: ActiveRecord::Rollback is swallowed by the transaction block, so a nested service can roll back 'silently'; distinguish it from success explicitly.
After a rollback the in-memory objects keep their assigned attributes - the database is restored, the objects are not.
Enqueuing background work inside the transaction can run jobs before the rows are visible; use after_commit for anything that leaves the boundary.
